_doc: Real administrative geography of Angola (Lei n.º 14/24). Contains only records this project can cite (docs/GEOGRAPHY.md). It is NOT the playable world: playable locations are in playable.json and reference these ids. Internal ids (adm.*) never change; official_code holds the official code (Lei n.º 8/25) once verified and is null until then. Lists are partial: see 'complete' flags.

country.name: Angola
country.notes: Only provinces with a cited source are recorded (selected playable provinces plus new provinces named in the sources). The remaining provinces must be added from a source that lists them (Lei 14/24 annex). Installation of the new provinces is gradual and continues after the 2027 elections; land-right concessions in the new provinces were suspended during the transition.

sources.confirms: Lei n.º 14/24, de 5 de Setembro: Angola is constituted by 21 provinces, 326 municipalities and 378 comunas.
Parliament approved the division into 21 provinces (August 2024); entry into force planned for January 2025.
Decreto Presidencial n.º 268/24 approves the action plan and timetable for implementing the new division.
Effective installation of the new division extends beyond the 2027 elections.
In December 2024 the government suspended the granting of land rights in the three new provinces during the administrative transition.
Icolo e Bengo arises from the division of Luanda province; Luanda remains a province.
Administrators were appointed for the 16 municipalities of Luanda after the new division came into force.

Lists the current municipalities of Luanda province (15 names: Cacuaco, Cazenga, Viana, Belas, Kilamba Kiaxi, Sambizanga, Rangel, Kilamba, Talatona, Camama, Maianga, Hoji Ya Henda, Ingombota, Samba, Mulenvos).
Province created on 5 September 2024 from Luanda province; seat Catete; seven municipalities: Bom Jesus, Cabiri, Cabo Ledo, Calumbo, Catete, Quiçama, Sequele.
The first governor of Icolo e Bengo took office (December 2024).
Icolo e Bengo is one of the new provinces, arising from the division of Luanda.
Benguela province went from 10 to 23 municipalities under the new division, in force 1 January 2025; names the 13 new ones.
Provincial government portal lists the original municipalities: Baía Farta, Balombo, Bocoio, Caimbambo, Catumbela, Chongorói, Cubal, Ganda, Lobito and Benguela.

provinces.name: Huíla
provinces.count_note: Search excerpts disagreed (14 to 21, or 23 including the nine new municipalities). Unresolved.

sources.confirms: Since 1 January 2025 Huíla has nine new municipalities (Hoque, Galangue, Palanca, Capelongo, Capunda Cavilongo, Viti Vivali, Chicungo, Dongo, Chituto), formerly comunas of existing municipalities.
Lubango is the capital of Huíla province.
Six comunas (Alto-Hama, Bimbe, Cuima, Chilata, Galanga, Sambo) became municipalities, carved from Bailundo, Caála, Chicala-Cholohanga, Londuimbali and Longonjo; the province has 17 municipalities.
Government portal page for Huambo province lists 17 municipalities.
After Lei n.º 14/24 the province has 9 municipalities and 11 comunas (previously 5 municipalities and 16 comunas).
Lists Moçâmedes (capital) and Tômbwa among Namibe's municipalities.

Cabinda went from four to ten municipalities: Cabinda, Cacongo, Buco-Zau, Belize, Miconje, Massabi, Necuto, Tando-Zinze, Liambo, Ngoio (list as quoted in search excerpts of the provincial government's 2025 news).

provinces.name: Malanje
provinces.count_note: 27 = 14 previous + 13 new (ANGOP reports 13 new municipalities from 1 January 2025).

sources.confirms: Malanje province officially has 13 new municipalities from 1 January 2025 under the new division.
The governor appointed administrators for 11 of the 13 new municipalities.
Cuando arises from the division of the former Cuando Cubango province.
A province named Moxico Leste was created from the division of Moxico.
A new province arises from the division of Moxico; one Ver Angola article names it 'Cassai Zambeze'.
From 1 January 2025 the urban districts of Rangel, Samba, Maianga, Ingombota and Sambizanga became municipalities of Luanda.
Maianga is listed among the municipalities of Luanda province.
Ingombota became a municipality of Luanda from 1 January 2025.
Ingombota is listed among the municipalities of Luanda province.
The Centralidade do Kilamba is among the new municipalities of Luanda.
Kilamba (distinct from Kilamba Kiaxi) is listed among the municipalities of Luanda province.
Talatona is listed among the municipalities of Luanda province. (One search summary claimed this article omits Talatona; the quoted list includes it.)
Talatona is a municipality of Luanda province (communes Talatona and Benfica); page not dated after the reform.
Cazenga is listed among the municipalities of Luanda province.
Catete is one of the seven municipalities and the seat of Icolo e Bengo.
Catete is named among the municipal administrative seats of Icolo e Bengo.
Sequele is one of the seven municipalities of Icolo e Bengo.
The territory of Icolo e Bengo includes Sequele (and its centralidade).
Calumbo is one of the seven municipalities of Icolo e Bengo.
Calumbo is the most populous municipality (Censo 2024: 652,270, including Zango).
Cabo Ledo is one of the seven municipalities of Icolo e Bengo.
Cabo Ledo municipality: 23,089 residents (Censo 2024).
Bom Jesus is one of the seven municipalities of Icolo e Bengo.
Bom Jesus is named among the municipal administrative seats of Icolo e Bengo.
Lobito is listed among Benguela's municipalities.
The new municipality Egipto-Praia was formed from a comuna of Lobito; Lobito remains a municipality.
Benguela is listed among Benguela's municipalities.
Catumbela is listed among Benguela's municipalities.
The new municipality Biópio was formed from a comuna of Catumbela; Catumbela remains a municipality.
Baía Farta is listed among Benguela's municipalities.
The new municipality Dombe Grande was formed from a comuna of Baía Farta; Baía Farta remains a municipality.
Lubango (formerly Sá da Bandeira) is a municipality in Angola and the capital of Huíla province.
The new municipality Hoque was formerly a comuna of Lubango.
The new municipality Palanca was formerly a comuna of Humpata (a municipality of Huíla).

municipalities.name: Huambo
municipalities.status_note: The city of Huambo is verified, but no source read in this session explicitly states that a municipality named Huambo exists after the reform. The new municipalities came from Bailundo, Caála, Chicala-Cholohanga, Londuimbali and Longonjo (not from a Huambo municipality).

sources.confirms: Lists the municipalities the six new ones were carved from; a Huambo municipality is not among them.
Caála is a municipality of Huambo; the new municipality Cuima was carved from it.
Caála appears in the government's table of Huambo municipalities (comunas Caála, Catata, Calenga).
Moçâmedes is a municipality and the capital of Namibe.
Government portal lists Moçâmedes as a municipality of Namibe (with comunas Moçâmedes, Lucira, Bentiaba, Forte Santa Rita).
Tômbwa is a municipality of Namibe.
Government portal lists the municipality as 'Tômbua' (comunas Baía dos Tigres, Iona, Tômbua; may predate the reform).
Cabinda is one of the ten municipalities of Cabinda province.
Cacongo is one of the ten municipalities of Cabinda province.
Buco-Zau is one of the ten municipalities of Cabinda province.
Tando-Zinze is one of the ten municipalities of Cabinda province (former comuna, elevated in 2025).
The population of Tando-Zinze received its first municipal administrator (February 2025).

municipalities.name: Malanje
municipalities.status_note: The city of Malanje is verified, but no source read in this session states the post-reform municipality of Malanje or whether any city areas moved to new municipalities.

sources.confirms: Malanje is the capital city of Malanje province (city, not the post-reform municipality).
Calandula appears with an appointed municipal administrator in Malanje province.
Calandula is one of the municipalities of Malanje province; the Calandula falls are near the city (pre-reform list).

comunas.name: Forte Santa Rita
comunas.status_note: Listed as a comuna of Moçâmedes by the government portal, whose data may predate the 2025 reform (Namibe now has 11 comunas). Current status needs confirmation.

sources.confirms: Forte Santa Rita is listed as a comuna of the municipality of Moçâmedes.

comunas.name: Lândana
comunas.status_note: Listed as a comuna of Cacongo by the government portal, which may be out of date (several new municipalities shown without administrators). Current status needs confirmation.

sources.confirms: Cacongo has the comunas Dinge and Lândana.

pending_proposals.summary: An adjustment report describes splitting Malanje into Malanje Norte (capital Calandula; Calandula, Cacuso, Massango, Marimba, Quela, Cahombo, Kunda dya Baze, Kiwaba Nzoji) and Malanje Sul.
pending_proposals.note: Not reflected in the 21-province law; recorded only so it is not mistaken for current geography.

sources.confirms: Reports a DPA adjustment document describing Malanje Norte and Malanje Sul; does not show a published law.
